subject.title: [Feature]:Support per-agent command lanes for multi-agent deployments

question: What public scheduler/config contract should OpenClaw use for foreground per-agent command lane isolation on shared gateways?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding per-agent foreground lanes changes public configuration and scheduler resource semantics, and the prior PR showed security and compatibility pitfalls around request-controlled lanes and lane-specific caps.

options.title: Design a unified lane-routing model
options.body: Keep this issue as the foreground-agent scheduling case and design a trusted config model that can also accommodate hook, channel/browser, and subagent lane routing without request-controlled lane minting.

options.title: Ship a narrow per-agent option
options.body: Add a default-off per-agent or per-agent-group foreground lane setting with explicit aggregate caps, docs, and upgrade-safe defaults while leaving other lane surfaces separate.

options.title: Document deployment partitioning only
options.body: Decline new core lane configuration for now and document separate gateway processes as the supported isolation boundary for heavy agents.

recommendation.title: Design a unified lane-routing model
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the foreground-agent scheduling case and design a trusted config model that can also accommodate hook, channel/browser, and subagent lane routing without request-controlled lane minting.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest available history across embedded runner lanes and gateway lane concurrency, and is the best routing candidate for the scheduler/config contract decision.
